The start and end time for this event is based on the second landslide signal seen in Fig. 2, Chadwick and others (2012). Chadwick and others (2012) note: "The durations of the landslide signals at NW Rota-1 (minutes to hours) are also consistent with the recordings at Stromboli and Kilauea (Caplan-Auerbach et al., 2001; La Rocca et al., 2004). However, the multiple pulses and their long overall duration indicate that the NW Rota-1 landslide was not a single event, but instead involved an extended sequence of retrogressive failures."

An alternate seismic interpretation of this event comes from Haney and Wech (written commun., 2021). The seismic data from GUMO-BHZ filtered between 0.025 and 0.04 Hz shows a long-period signal between approximately 16:56 (UTC) and 17:06 (UTC).
